reasoning: The holder writes HOLDER_READY after acquiring the FILE_COMMON fence, but the runner does not prove that the holder tester process or fence handle is still alive at the exact moment the probe attempts FileOpen.

R2_HOLDER and R2_PROBE use a one-day Strategy Tester interval. The tester can finish that interval faster than the requested 180000 ms wall-clock hold, which triggers OnDeinit and ReleaseFence before the probe starts.

The runner checks only the persistent HOLDER_READY marker before launching the probe; it has no holder heartbeat, process-liveness assertion, or lock-token observation immediately before and during probe execution.

Failure code 52 conflates an explicit probe FAIL with missing/unreadable probe evidence because the fail path does not snapshot the probe result or holder lifecycle artifacts. The uploaded ZIP contains neither HOLDER_READY, probe result, holder release result nor tester runtime logs, so exact concurrent state is not recoverable from evidence.

Therefore the evidence does not establish that two simultaneously live MQL processes could acquire the same no-share FILE_COMMON file. It only establishes that the R2 qualifier did not observe a PASS from its fencing probe.

required_r2_repair: Make the holder prove real overlap: publish a monotonically refreshed heartbeat/token while the lock handle remains open, or use a bounded real-wall-clock busy hold that cannot finish the tester interval before the probe.
Before probe launch require holder process alive AND fresh heartbeat AND expected lock token; after probe require holder still alive/fresh until probe evidence is snapshotted.
Use separate result files for HOLDER, PROBE and REACQUIRE; never reuse one RESULTS.csv for multiple modes.
On every failure snapshot all available holder/probe/reacquire CSVs plus isolated terminal/tester logs before cleanup.

Only classify FENCE_SECOND_EXECUTOR_NOT_DENIED when explicit probe evidence says SECOND_LOCK_ACQUIRED while a fresh holder heartbeat proves the first handle was still owned. Missing evidence must receive a separate fail code.
